abstract:
Official code of paper "DeeR-VLA: Dynamic Inference of Multimodal Large Language Models for Efficient Robot Execution"

DeeR-VLA: Dynamic Inference of Multimodal Large Language Models for Efficient Robot Execution ( NeurIPS 24 ) Yang Yue 1   Yulin Wang 1   Bingyi Kang 2   Yizeng Han 1   Shenzhi Wang 1   Shiji Song 1   Jiashi Feng 2   Gao Huang 1 1 Tsinghua University   2 ByteDance Research [ ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.02359) [ ](https://huggingface.co/Yang130/DeeR-VLA/tree/main) ## Overview This is also the official code repository for the paper [DeeR-VLA](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.02359). DeeR-VLA is a framework for dynamic inference of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) designed specifically for efficient robot execution. Developing MLLMs for real-world robots is challenging due to the typically limited computation and memory capacities available on robotic platforms. DeeR-VLA addresses this challenge by implementing a Dynamic Early-Exit strategy that automatically adjusts the size of the activated MLLM based on the complexity of each situation. This approach leverages a multi-exit architecture, allowing the model to terminate processing once an appropriate size has been activated, thus avoiding redundant computation. DeeR-VLA also incorporates novel algorithms to establish early-termination criteria based on predefined demands such as average computational cost, peak computational consumption, and GPU memory usage. On the CALVIN robot manipulation benchmark, DeeR demonstrates significant reductions in computational costs of LLM by 5.2-6.5x and GPU memory of LLM by 2-6x without compromising performance. ### Performance on CALVIN Benchmark ## Installation 1. Install [CALVIN](https://github.com/mees/calvin) simulator in your python environment following the instructions. Then download dataset `D`, `ABC`, and `ABCD`. 2. Clone DeeR-VLA: 3. Install dependencies in virtual environment: 4. Download the following models from Hugging Face. abstract_zh: 本文是论文“DeeR-VLA：面向高效机器人执行的多模态大语言模型动态推理”（NeurIPS 24）的官方代码库。DeeR-VLA是一个专为高效机器人执行而设计的动态推理框架，用于多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）。由于机器人平台通常计算和内存资源有限，开发用于真实世界机器人的MLLMs具有挑战性。DeeR-VLA通过实现一种动态早退策略来解决这一挑战，该策略根据每个情境的复杂度自动调整激活的MLLM的大小。该方法利用多出口架构，一旦激活了适当大小的模型即可终止处理，从而避免冗余计算。DeeR-VLA还引入了新颖的算法，基于预定义的需求（如平均计算成本、峰值计算消耗和GPU内存使用）建立早停标准。在CALVIN机器人操作基准上，DeeR在保持性能的同时，显著降低了LLM的计算成本（5.2-6.5倍）和GPU内存（2-6倍）。
tldr_zh: DeeR-VLA通过动态早退策略，在机器人任务中大幅降低计算和内存开销，且不损性能。

>[!abstract] 一句话总结：提出DeeR-VLA框架，通过动态早退（Dynamic Early-Exit）策略和多出口架构，根据当前情境复杂度自动调整激活的MLLM规模，并设计基于预定义计算预算（平均计算开销、峰值消耗、GPU内存）的终止判据。


# 一、动机

> 机器人平台上的计算和内存资源有限，而多模态大语言模型（MLLM）直接部署在真实机器人上效率低下，现有方法无法根据任务复杂度动态调整模型计算量。


# 二、方法

> 提出DeeR-VLA框架，通过动态早退（Dynamic Early-Exit）策略和多出口架构，根据当前情境复杂度自动调整激活的MLLM规模，并设计基于预定义计算预算（平均计算开销、峰值消耗、GPU内存）的终止判据。


# 三、核心实验结果

> 在CALVIN机器人操作基准上，LLM计算成本降低5.2-6.5倍，GPU内存降低2-6倍，且不损失任务性能。


# 四、对我的启发

> 该工作为MLLM在资源受限机器人平台上的高效部署提供了新思路，动态推理机制可推广到其他具身智能任务；但当前仅验证了仿真环境，真实硬件上的延迟与功耗收益有待进一步测试。
